findings.what: When H2 is on (the demo default), F1E's NOT_READY LatestExit is now the H2 horizon for every F1E position, held or not. If ETH stays NOT_READY for more than 10 minutes after a load, an F1E position whose paper trade ended at 15:55 New York (not held) is not closed at that time. It stays on its broker stop until ETH is READY (then an ORPHAN close) or until the horizon, which can be two business days later. SPEC 4.8 gives the horizon for F1E and SPEC 9.16 gives the 10-minute wait. Neither says that unheld F1E trades also get the 2-day horizon.
findings.evidence: rc_f1c.py: F1E long 155600280006, filled 2019-04-23 07:00 UTC, paper exit 19:55 UTC, not held. One restart at 18:00 UTC with ETH unsynchronized for 54 h. New file: no close at 19:55. Its broker stop closed it at 22:16:59 UTC (-295.18 EUR). Without the stop it would have stayed open until Thursday 2019-04-25 19:55 UTC. Reviewed file 1ca53085c0c1: CLOSE why=latest_exit at 19:55:02 (-205.09 EUR). Code: CR_Rule_F1.mqh LatestExit (if(m_h2) x0 = max(x0, F1H2Horizon(t_dec))) and CR_Follower.mqh FolNotReadyExits. Ordinary restarts are not affected: READY comes 2 s to 3 min after the load, and the reconcile then follows the paper (see the reproduction notes).

Before real money (H2 is off on real by default), either write the trade-off into SPEC 9.16, or change the rule: after the 10-minute wait, close an F1E+H2 position at 15:55 New York (gap rule) unless it passes H2's own hold test from broker data, side x (quote - POSITION_PRICE_OPEN) >= 1.0 x |POSITION_PRICE_OPEN - POSITION_SL|. F1's stop never moves after its PFILL, so the test can be read from the position.

findings.what: The new 'shut minute' rule (BarsShut) blocks real orders both in masked minutes and inside the built-in XAU holiday closures. The mask, however, keeps gold bars that fall inside those closures, so the paper can fill where the robot will not send. SPEC 9.17 says the paper 'never keeps such a bar' and so agrees. That is true for masked minutes, but not for closures.
findings.evidence: check/out/clock/xau_holiday_scan.csv: 89 in-sample gold bars on 22 holiday dates fall inside the built-in closures (for example 2019-07-04 13:00-16:56 New York, 19 bars on 2013-05-27) and are kept bars. BarsShut = BarsMaskReason != KEPT || ClkInClosure (CR_Bars.mqh). I scanned my whole-EA replay with switches off and on: 0 gold paper fills on, or one minute before, such a bar. So no in-sample trade differs. The effect is conservative: a missed trade (MISSED reason=market_shut), never an unwanted order.
findings.fix: Correct SPEC 9.17: if the broker quotes gold inside a built-in closure, the robot misses trades the paper takes. Alternatively, let BarsShut use only the mask and let the broker's own session refuse orders during a real closure.

findings.what: Two limits of the mock (not defects of the robot) weaken part of the evidence. (a) The mock's saved state keeps only the first word of each position and deal comment. In all ~2,000 T6 restarts the EA therefore sees 'CR' instead of 'CR <code> <decision>', and the LatestExit comment cross-check is never run after a restart. (b) Scripted deals (MOCK_DEALS) are booked only at the next minute start. A GUARD, STOP or LOCK triggered by a deal inside an intent's retry window therefore cannot be tested. The only F4 world (block_resend) uses the Friday close, a block that depends on the clock alone.
findings.evidence: mock_replay.h rp_load_state reads comments with %255s. My F1 runs show 'CR F1E 1803141000' in the continuous run and 'CR' after the restart. rc_f4.py: a -60,000 EUR manual loss booked at 02:00:03 UTC, inside BKB's retry window (F3S preset, guard on), reaches the ledger only at 02:01:02. The new file and the reviewed file both open at 02:00:09 and both are closed by the guard at 02:01:02, so this world cannot tell them apart. In MT5 the deal's OnTradeTransaction makes the ledger re-read at the next 100 ms pass, and the ledger stays settled because balance and history move together.
findings.fix: In the mock, save comments with a delimiter that keeps spaces, and book scripted deals at their exact second. Then add an F4 world with a GUARD or STOP latch inside the retry window.

findings.what: The MetaEditor compile is still unproven (F12; SPEC 10.1 stays the gate). Nothing in this round's diff is outside the MQL5 subset or looks likely to be refused. The new code adds a default constructor in CRuleF1, ternaries with string literals, datetime % int and plain globals. Two risk points remain from before this round: a struct member named 'group' ('group' is used by MQL5's 'input group' syntax), and 4 implicit long-to-double conversions in MathAbs((long)...).
findings.evidence: to_cpp.py accepts the dist: no ->, new, virtual, template, function macros, Sleep, fmax/fmin or #import. g++ -Wall gives 0 warnings in my harness, release and sanitizer builds. g++ -Wextra -Wshadow -Wconversion gives the same 4 long-to-double warnings as the reviewed file and nothing new. clang++ -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow-all gives 0.
